title: Function Calling Deep Dive — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini
service: FCBridge: one canonical tool-calling model translated at the edge for OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini, with a SQLite conversation store, per-provider request rendering, a cross-provider equivalence probe and an OpenAI strict-mode schema compiler
runtime: Python 3.10+, standard library, pytest; no network: scripted fake providers in the tests check each request the way the lesson says the real API would

parts.lesson_anchor: Shape diffs (Required / Any, Force-a-tool); Limits you will actually hit (depth 5, practical limit 10); code/main.py _gemini_schema, tool_choice_anthropic, parse_openai; quiz Q4, Q5, Q9, Q10
planted_bugs: tool_choice_anthropic folds auto, none and required into one tuple check copied from tool_choice_openai, so required becomes {type: required}; the fake Anthropic API rejects the whole request, two calls from the root (Bridge.ask -> tool_fields -> tool_choice_anthropic)

_gemini_schema upper-cases only string types (the lesson's own code), so WEATHER's [string, null] goes out as a list; the fake Gemini API rejects functionDeclarations[0].parameters.properties.units.type three calls from the root; the fix writes one upper-case type plus nullable: true and raises ValueError for a union of two real types (quiz Q9.3)
parse_openai hands the empty arguments string of a no-parameter tool to json.loads (JSONDecodeError); it means no arguments, and raw_arguments keeps ''
schema_depth recurses twice per child, once in the comparison and once for the value, so the work doubles at every nested hop
parts.timing_assert: schema_depth of a folder tree 10 folders deep (object -> array -> object ...) under 0.03 s; measured on this machine (Apple M5) with and without other jobs running: the double recursion 0.31-0.59 s on Python 3.12 (0.34-0.44 s on 3.14, 0.45-0.92 s on 3.10), the single recursion 0.015-0.11 ms
parts.overfix_guard: a property named type and a [null, string] type order (translating every type key crashes on the property, taking the first list entry gives NULL); invalid JSON arguments still raise ValueError (swallowing the error as {} would run the tool with no arguments); exact depths 8 and 12 with per-provider limits (OpenAI rejects 8, OpenAI and Anthropic reject 12, Gemini has no limit), which rules out capping the recursion at OpenAI's or Anthropic's limit to make it fast

deviations: Part 1: the four suggested defects are kept. The timing case is a folder tree 10 deep (object -> array -> object) rather than the suggested 12-level chain, because the double recursion costs about 2^hops: a 12-level object chain takes about 2 ms even with the bug. Ten deep keeps the slow version under a second on a loaded machine (an 11-deep tree takes 1.4-2 s, and up to 9 s at load average 310). The 8- and 12-level chains stay as the exactness guard. The Gemini fix also raises ValueError for a union of two real types (quiz Q9.3), and a property named type plus a [null, string] order guard the naive fixes. Both the Anthropic and the Gemini errors surface in fake providers that check requests.

Part 1: tool_fields (declarations plus tool choice, with every Gemini declaration in one functionDeclarations object) is working code, because Bridge.ask needs it; Part 3's Gemini trap moves from that wrapper to the tool count, where 64 counts functions and not the single tool object.

Part 2: the round trip also compares JSON text, which catches SQLite's 0/1 for is_error and sorted keys. Integers beyond 2^53 (2^64 + 1) are in the fixture, but Python's json keeps them exactly, so they only bite a store that puts numbers in SQLite INTEGER columns (OverflowError above 2^63) or reads them through SQLite's JSON functions (REAL). The rowid trap needs a write in the middle of a conversation: replace() redacts a tool result in place.

Part 3: non-OpenAI calls go to OpenAI as json_text (UTF-8, no \u escapes, a given helper), which makes the byte limit exact: the arguments text of {"summary": 2725 CJK characters plus "ab"} is exactly 8192 bytes but 2742 characters, and 16367 bytes with \u escapes.

Part 4: statuses are ok, error and timeout; the summary is same, different or incomplete, and different wins over a failure. A refusal and a reply with two calls are error records, and the timed-out request must be cancelled. Lesson 03's streaming reassembly and parallel execution are not used.

Part 5: besides inlining, additionalProperties and nullable optionals, an optional anyOf gains a null branch, an enum next to a nullable type gains None (WEATHER's units, quiz Q7), the input stays unchanged and copies share nothing (the test mutates one). A schema deeper than OpenAI's 5 once inlined raises LimitError.
